maria (Support): FYI ticket #4321 — customer says their app started getting 403s to our /v1/generate at ~08:15 UTC. They use Private (VPC) with egress allowlist on their side.
kevin (SRE): I see a spike of 403s from that org in our logs at 08:14-08:20. Error body says 'client IP not allowlisted'.
ashwin (Eng-Infra): can you paste a sample request/response? need to confirm it's egress IP mismatch not TLS/auth.
maria (Support): pasted below — customer provided curl output:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "ip_not_allowlisted",
  "message": "request received from 34.120.8.99 which is not on the customer's allowlist"
}
```
kevin (SRE): That IP (34.120.8.99) is in our recent NAT pool for the region. We rolled a small NAT rotation during scheduled maintenance at 08:00 UTC — looks like this customer still has old IPs allowlisted. Old: 34.120.5.12, 34.120.5.13. New: 34.120.8.98, 34.120.8.99.
ashwin (Eng-Infra): Confirmed on infra side — rotation was intentional to drain a host. No TLS/cert changes. No auth changes.
egress-rotation-bot: [automated] NAT pool rotation executed: pool-nyc-3, affected subnets: 10.2.0.0/16, change window 08:00-08:10 UTC. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/egress-rotation
sylvie (CSE): Okay — customer-facing plan: ask them to add the new egress IPs to their allowlist and retry. Offer a temporary workaround: use our dedicated static-egress option or route through a proxy with fixed IPs.
maria (Support): I'll send the update with exact IPs and repro steps. Also asked them to retry and paste a failing curl if it persists.
kevin (SRE): For quicker troubleshooting, ask customer to run `dig +short myip.opendns.com @resolver1.opendns.com` from their app host behind the VPC to surface what their traffic egresses as (sometimes customer-side NAT does another SNAT).
sylvie (CSE): Also recommend lowering DNS TTLs on their firewall allowlist if they use DNS-based allowlisting — TTL drift can cause delays after rotations.
maria (Support): Customer replied — they updated allowlist with new IPs and confirm calls are green. I'll close the ticket after 24h monitoring.
kevin (SRE): Follow-up action for us: add a short notification to customers who have egress allowlists when we schedule NAT rotations. Maybe an email / console banner. Filing a small internal ticket.
ashwin (Eng-Infra): +1. Also adding these IPs to our public doc that lists 'recent egress addresses' so customers can pull programmatically.
sylvie (CSE): Thanks team, nice triage. maria pls mark incident type "egress-allowlist-drift" so we can track frequency.
maria (Support): will do. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
